mostWorthwhile.text: Building the air–blood exchange surface was most worthwhile: the planned pressure comparisons explain why oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse in opposite directions rather than treating exchange as a single process.

leastWorthwhile.text: The attempt to attach bronchioles directly to the supported exchange surface was frustrating: their pictured ends seemed to match, but the result did not explain why the larger airway tree had to be assembled first.

surprise.text: The sacs required surfactant before the capillary sheet could be added. The explanation connected that prerequisite to keeping small sacs from collapsing.

arbitrary.text: The required order of airway assembly felt somewhat arbitrary: the bronchioles appeared positioned to meet the exchange region, yet only the completed conducting tree could connect to it.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the constructions connect structure to function, particularly gas diffusion and airway resistance. The picture plans are useful explanations, though they are not finished illustrations.
